name: NormalityChecker.Localized.discrepancy_rate

doc: Each of the five accumulated residues. Grid points 6 and 7 are in the same cell.
label: decimal_residue_table
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.decimal_residue_table

doc: Reindex the positive series by its three independent prime exponents.
label: decimal_value_eq_series
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.decimal_value_eq_series

doc: More than one off-base prime. These tests certify the selected denominator prime.
label: binary_certificates
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.binary_certificates

doc: The shifted omitted tail is bounded uniformly by `1/(n+1)`.
label: shift_error
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.shift_error

doc: On a stretch without an insertion the shifted rational prefix follows the base orbit exactly.
label: prefix_orbit
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.prefix_orbit

doc:
Exact exponent of five in the reduced denominator. One factor cancels precisely
on the middle cell, and no second factor ever cancels.
label: denominator_fives
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedFive.denominator_fives

doc:
A scalar criterion for a shared mask lifts to a joint theorem for distinct
positive pole orders and arbitrary rational polynomial numerators nonzero at zero.
label: joint_of_masked_poles
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.joint_of_masked_poles

doc:
Rational Laurent weights of distinct exact pole orders on a common full
finite prime support give simultaneous rectangle frequencies.
label: joint_full_polynomial_orders
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.joint_full_polynomial_orders

doc:
On a single off-radix prime axis the same vector theorem holds on every
unbounded common mask. The gaps between retained exponents may be unbounded.
label: joint_infinite_axis_orders
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.joint_infinite_axis_orders

doc:
For a nonempty vector on a single off-radix prime axis, unboundedness
of the shared mask is necessary and sufficient for joint uniformity.
label: joint_axis_orders_iff
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.joint_axis_orders_iff

doc:
In odd radix, on any finite prime support containing two, a common mask may
vary arbitrarily away from the sufficiently late powers of two.
label: joint_late_twos_orders
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.joint_late_twos_orders

doc:
Paper II, Corollary 1.3. Joint visits of the distinct unsigned orders to
every half-open rectangle converge to the product of its side lengths.
label: joint_full_orders
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.joint_full_orders

doc: The independent positive-index series and direct position count satisfy the corollary.
label: distinct_orders_checked
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.distinct_orders_checked

doc:
Between two cutoffs of ratio at most `q`, distinct new insertions have distinct
`p`-exponents. The left endpoint is excluded and the right endpoint is included.
label: layers_injective
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.layers_injective

doc:
An insertion with exponent `j` forces at least one of the two endpoint prefixes
to have `p`-adic norm at least `p^j`, regardless of all the other insertions.
label: separated_prefixes
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.separated_prefixes

doc:
Away from recent insertions the cofactor dividing the base has cleared,
and the remaining denominator divides the largest available power of `p`.
label: clean_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.clean_denominator

doc:
With two independent cofactors 2 and 5 in base 10, the insertions at
`4*3^j` and `5*3^j` share the highest new layer on `(3*3^j,5*3^j]`.
Their combined numerator after removing that layer has exactly two factors
of three for `j ≥ 1`.
label: decimal_layer_collision
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.decimal_layer_collision

doc:
The first missing positive index determines the approximation error within
an absolute factor of two, independent of every other prime in the support.
label: first_omission_bounds
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.first_omission_bounds

doc:
Every open interval above one contains a threshold `q^a / p^i` with both
exponents natural. This uses the forward orbit of an irrational rotation.
label: threshold_between
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.threshold_between

doc:
Uniform finite precision: the top `J+1` layers meet every subinterval of
width at least `ε` in a unit cell. `J` is independent of the large scale.
label: threshold_mesh
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.threshold_mesh

doc:
On each unit cell of the normalized scale, any two exceptional positions are
less than `ε p^k` apart. This includes cutoffs inside the exceptional region.
label: exceptional_diameter_of_mesh
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.exceptional_diameter_of_mesh

doc: A set of integer starts of diameter at most `w` has at most `w+1` members.
label: card_of_diameter
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.card_of_diameter

doc:
For every exceptional fraction `ε`, all sufficiently large loss thresholds `L`
have exceptional fraction at most `ε` on all sufficiently late prime-power shells.
The denominator is the reduced denominator at *every* digit position.
label: severe_loss_rare
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.severe_loss_rare

doc:
One positive return of the irrational rotation with explicit upper and lower
step sizes. The lower bound uses only that distinct positive integers differ by one.
label: mesh_return
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.mesh_return

doc:
A threshold occurs in every interval of width `3 U log(q)/(M+1)` in
`[1,U]`, using a layer at most `M*q^2*p^M`. All exponents are natural.
label: effective_threshold_mesh
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.effective_threshold_mesh

doc:
The cost of an arbitrary partial cell consists of a vanishing block error
and the specified exceptional width. Only starts with a small denominator are charged.
label: statistic_cell_bound
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.statistic_cell_bound

doc:
Mixed two-generator normality in base `b`, for `q ∣ b` and an odd prime
`p` coprime to `b`. The hypotheses allow composite `q` as well.
label: normal
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.normal

doc: The literal double series for every compatible base, including composite `q ∣ b`.
label: series_normal
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.series_normal

doc: The binary logarithmic series restricted to `{2,p}` is normal for every odd prime `p`.
label: binary_series_normal
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.binary_series_normal

doc:
The binary localized logarithm supported on the primes two and five is normal.
The scale cells have length `K^6` for `K = 5^k`; their exceptional blocks
occupy at most a polynomial in `k` times `K^5` positions.
label: binary_normal
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedFive.binary_normal

doc: Normality for the literal nested series, without any project-specific constant.
label: series_binary_normal
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedFive.series_binary_normal

doc: Literal double-series statement, reindexed by unique factorization.
label: value_eq_series
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedFive.value_eq_series

doc: The omitted positive tail is dominated by the ordinary logarithm tail at the same shift.
label: shift_error
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedFive.shift_error

doc: On an interval with no new supported index the rational prefix evolves by doubling alone.
label: prefix_orbit
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedFive.prefix_orbit

doc:
Once all inserted dyadic denominators have cleared, the whole reduced denominator
is a power of five dividing the largest available power.
label: clean_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedFive.clean_denominator

doc:
For an arbitrary signed rational residue weight, normality at order one on a
single off-radix prime axis is decided by the finite windows of its eventual power cycle.
label: periodic_axis_normal_iff
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.periodic_axis_normal_iff

doc:
Every numerator on the ternary axis is nonzero, but the weights alternate
between 1 and -3. A recurring zero window prevents binary normality.
label: periodic_axis_counterexample
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.periodic_axis_counterexample

doc: The shifted omitted tail is bounded uniformly by `1/(n+1)`.
label: shift_error
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.shift_error

doc: A normalized polynomial combines shifted models for any radix moment identity.
label: polynomial_moment_error
name: NormalityChecker.polynomial_moment_error

doc:
Exact error for every digit position and every normalized rational polynomial.
The rational model is executable directly from the coefficients.
label: polynomial_log_error
name: NormalityChecker.polynomial_log_error

doc: The same construction on the BBP integral, normalized at sixteen.
label: polynomial_bbp_error
name: NormalityChecker.polynomial_bbp_error

doc: At position zero the quotient integral itself is the rational model.
label: polynomial_log_rational_integral
name: NormalityChecker.polynomial_log_rational_integral

doc:
Unrestricted rational coefficients attain every rational target at any one
start. The arithmetic content of a search lies in its independent error bound.
label: normalized_kernel_for_target
name: NormalityChecker.normalized_kernel_for_target

doc: An explicit rational enclosure, uniform in the shift n and in the power d.
label: chebyshev_log_error
name: NormalityChecker.chebyshev_log_error

doc: The remaining one-step error has an explicit sign and factorial quotient.
label: logShadow_step
name: NormalityChecker.logShadow_step

doc:
Uniform local error on a block. Its constants are explicit even when `r`
is chosen as a function of the starting position.
label: logShadow_orbit_bound
name: NormalityChecker.logShadow_orbit_bound

doc:
A rational model shadows all actual rational prefixes on `[n,2n]` with
unwrapped error at most `3/(n+1)`. No smoothness assumption on its denominator.
label: logPrefix_linear_shadow
name: NormalityChecker.logPrefix_linear_shadow

doc:
Divide the block error by `2^i` and let the block grow. The endpoint error
in the actual logarithm stays bounded, yielding exponential accuracy at the start.
label: logTwo_corrected_tail
name: NormalityChecker.logTwo_corrected_tail

doc: The factorial corrections are moments of the error of a finite geometric series.
label: logShadow_integral
name: NormalityChecker.logShadow_integral

doc:
The diagonal error is bounded by a beta integral, retaining the factor
that tends to zero even after `2*n` further shifts.
label: logShadow_beta_bound
name: NormalityChecker.logShadow_beta_bound

doc:
The same rational model shadows the inclusive endpoint at `2*n` further
shifts. The squared unwrapped error is at most `1/(n+1)`.
label: logShadow_double_length
name: NormalityChecker.logShadow_double_length

doc: The shifted infinite tail is nonnegative and at most `1/(n+1)`, for every `n`.
label: logTwo_tail_bounds
name: NormalityChecker.logTwo_tail_bounds

doc:
The binary normality problem for the logarithm is exactly a distribution problem
for a sequence defined using rational arithmetic alone.
label: logTwo_normal_iff
name: NormalityChecker.logTwo_normal_iff

doc:
A run of `s+2` consecutive rational residues in `[0,1/4)`, starting at `n ≥ 1`,
forces `4 * 2^s < n+1`. This restricts run length, while allowing separated returns.
label: logPrefix_run_bound
name: NormalityChecker.logPrefix_run_bound

doc:
An unconditional dyadic approximation bound obtained from the auxiliary
integrals. All sufficiently late shifts stay at least 2^(-32n) from integers.
label: dyadic_separation
name: NormalityChecker.LogTwoForm.dyadic_separation

doc:
The one-sided recurrence forces a middle-third visit within two steps
of every sufficiently late digit transition, even near the period-two endpoints.
label: middle_hit_near_transition
name: NormalityChecker.middle_hit_near_transition

doc: Compare lower limits with a pointwise error that vanishes.
label: liminf_le_mul_of_error
name: NormalityChecker.liminf_le_mul_of_error

doc:
Every sufficiently late multiplicative window contains a visit of the
rational recurrence to the closed middle third and a true binary transition.
label: logTwo_window_hit
name: NormalityChecker.logTwo_window_hit

doc:
An unconditional logarithmic lower bound for both counts, with a fixed
additive offset. This gives infinitely many hits but leaves their lower density open.
label: logTwo_logarithmic_count
name: NormalityChecker.logTwo_logarithmic_count

doc: The unconditional finite-prefix discrepancy gap obtained from the count.
label: logTwo_finite_discrepancy_gap
name: NormalityChecker.logTwo_finite_discrepancy_gap

doc:
A finite zero list suffices: convergence of nonzero unshifted logarithm
series ensures that all their positive-index zero partial sums form such a list.
label: denominator_rate
name: NormalityChecker.LogarithmBands.denominator_rate

doc: Removing this particular representative clears p from the true reduced denominator.
label: primary_correct
name: NormalityChecker.LogarithmPrimaryCharacters.primary_correct

doc: Removing all selected primary terms simultaneously leaves a denominator prime to their product.
label: joint_remainder
name: NormalityChecker.LogarithmPrimaryCharacters.joint_remainder

doc:
Arbitrarily accurate real approximations can retain every odd-primary
component of any prescribed rational. Their denominators change by at most
a power of two in either direction.
label: dyadic_completion
name: NormalityChecker.LogarithmPrimaryCharacters.dyadic_completion

doc:
The diagonal and off-diagonal contributions to a block of characters.
A common unit-modulus twist leaves the pair correlations unchanged.
label: gram_bound
name: NormalityChecker.LogarithmPrimaryCharacters.gram_bound

doc:
A family of vectors with uniformly large aligned means must be small when
its off-diagonal correlations are small. The test vector can be any unit vector.
label: aligned_means
name: NormalityChecker.LogarithmPrimaryCharacters.aligned_means

doc:
A narrow interval meeting the central part of the orbit cannot contain
two consecutive shifts. Counting this case also handles intervals far from zero.
label: discrepancy_of_interior
name: NormalityChecker.Phase13.discrepancy_of_interior

doc: Pull a transition back through any number of binary shifts.
label: interior_before_transition
name: NormalityChecker.Phase13.interior_before_transition

doc:
For all sufficiently large k, every prefix of at least 68^(2k) shifts
has discrepancy gap at least k²/N. Taking k = floor((log base 68 of N)/2)
gives an unconditional squared-logarithm numerator at every large cutoff.
label: logTwo_squared_log_gap
name: NormalityChecker.Phase13.logTwo_squared_log_gap

doc: All sufficiently large prefixes, with the block length chosen as a function of N.
label: logTwo_all_prefix_gap
name: NormalityChecker.Phase13.logTwo_all_prefix_gap

doc:
Unnormalized Fourier costs on a tail interval: their square roots differ
by at most π sqrt(2/M), uniformly in the interval length.
label: logTwo_fourier_tail_stability
name: NormalityChecker.Phase13.logTwo_fourier_tail_stability

doc:
Clearing rational coefficients changes the reduced denominator exponent by
the valuation of the clearing integer. No assumption that it is prime to p is needed.
label: rational_den_exponent
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.rational_den_exponent

doc:
An isolated last retained power certifies every subsequent shift until the next
insertion, even when the next retained exponent is arbitrarily far away.
label: last_power_den_exponent
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.last_power_den_exponent

doc:
Every infinite mask on a single off-base prime-power axis is normal for
all rational polynomial weights with a pole at zero, of unrestricted degree.
label: infinite_axis_normal
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.infinite_axis_normal

doc:
Any eventually zero rational weight on a smooth support leaves a fixed grid
gap, including the empty mask.
label: finite_mask_nonnormal
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.finite_mask_nonnormal

doc:
Complete mask classification on one off-base prime-power axis in the
presence of a residual pole.
label: axis_normal_iff
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.axis_normal_iff

doc: Clearing coefficients commutes with every shifted, masked prefix.
label: normalized_prefix
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.normalized_prefix

doc:
Growth of denominators polynomial in the block length for rational weights
whose reduced denominators divide a fixed multiple of mᵗ.
label: clean_modulus
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.clean_modulus

doc: A finite collection of primes is absorbed by the radix and one coprime modulus.
label: offbase_modulus
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.offbase_modulus

doc:
Upper discrepancy for any selected family of late first cells, for the
rationally weighted number itself. Other retained smooth indices are arbitrary.
label: rational_window_bound
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.rational_window_bound

doc:
The lower density is attained along the left endpoints, for arbitrary gaps.
The ratio there is the sum of all preceding window lengths divided by uⱼ.
label: exact_window_density
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.exact_window_density

doc:
A single retained residue class has exact window density 1/(pʰ-1),
including arbitrary starting exponent.
label: residue_class_density
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.residue_class_density

doc:
Window density for arbitrary retained exponent sequences directly bounds the
discrepancy of the full series, regardless of the other retained indices.
label: discrepancy_of_density
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.discrepancy_of_density

doc:
Arbitrarily large jumps between successive retained exponents force lower
window density zero. This applies even if the support on that axis is normal.
label: unbounded_gaps_zero
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.unbounded_gaps_zero

doc: Finite selections have window density zero, including the empty selection.
label: finite_window_density
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.finite_window_density

doc:
The nonconstant part loses at least one full order of the pole, uniformly
over every mask at every position below p^(k+1).
label: lower_order_norm
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.lower_order_norm

doc:
If an unsigned prefix has e surviving factors of p and e exceeds the
lower-order budget plus vₚ(G(0)), the polynomial prefix retains at least e-vₚ(G(0)).
The conclusion is uniform over the retained subset.
label: leading_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.leading_denominator

doc:
Each executable unsigned certificate at the residual pole order also bounds the
discrepancy of the full rational polynomial series at that same precision.
label: polynomial_certificate_bound
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.polynomial_certificate_bound

doc:
Vanishing unsigned certificates imply normality for every rational polynomial
with the same residual pole order on the full smooth support.
label: normal_of_unsigned_certificates
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.normal_of_unsigned_certificates

doc:
The degree-ten polynomial in the notes, on any ternary/quinary/dyadic
smooth mask containing every sufficiently late power of two.
label: base_five_degree_ten
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.base_five_degree_ten

doc:
The same polynomial loses exactly two factors of two at each retained
dyadic scale k≥3. The statement concerns the actual rational prefix.
label: base_five_dyadic_exponent
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.base_five_dyadic_exponent

doc:
A rational polynomial having integer values after division by mˢ has
maximal discrepancy on every smooth mask, in every base.
label: consecutive_product_maximal
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.consecutive_product_maximal

doc:
The depth-two unsigned certificate for 5 and 13 proves binary normality
for every rational numerator nonzero at zero and a simple residual pole.
label: five_thirteen_polynomial_normal
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.five_thirteen_polynomial_normal

doc: A condition absent from every sufficiently large clean block has density zero.
label: exceptional_frequency
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.exceptional_frequency

doc: Concentration on the 1/L grid leaves a gap of length 1/L and precludes normality.
label: grid_discrepancy
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.grid_discrepancy

doc:
A common rational coefficient denominator with its radix part absorbed in bˡ.
If t=0 the smooth primes may be arbitrary.
label: grid_of_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.grid_of_denominator

doc:
Cancellation of the factor at zero holds term by term, for rational coefficients
and every mask, including all instances of a removable monomial denominator.
label: masked_cancel
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.masked_cancel

doc:
Full classification for integral polynomials. The root multiplicity is the
order of vanishing at zero and places no restriction on the total degree.
label: integer_full_classification
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.integer_full_classification

doc:
Closed count at every cell boundary. Its bounded offset from the periodic
limiting score is independent of the scale k.
label: period_endpoint
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.period_endpoint

doc:
The finite cell score is sharp for the window price, including cutoffs partway
through a geometric scale. This describes the price, independently of orbit quality.
label: exact_period_price
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.exact_period_price

doc:
Retaining exponents 0 and 1 modulo 3 at p=3 certifies exact window price
11/13 and therefore a discrepancy upper bound of 11/13.
label: ternary_period_price
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.ternary_period_price

doc:
Index-periodic masks induce an eventual period on the power exponents even
when the index modulus has a common factor with p.
label: index_mask_eventual_period
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.index_mask_eventual_period

doc:
For an eventually periodic exponent mask, the finite grid agrees with actual
retained windows at every sufficiently large position, in both directions.
label: periodic_windows
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.periodic_windows

doc:
Exact limsup of the missed-window fraction for the actual mask, allowing
all finite changes before periodicity begins. The complementary lower density is one minus this score.
label: periodic_mask_price
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.periodic_mask_price

doc:
A finite polynomial reciprocal on any finite list of integer units at p.
The product polynomial vanishes at each sampled denominator. Its divided difference
at zero represents their reciprocals with one common denominator prime to p.
label: finite_reciprocal
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.finite_reciprocal

doc:
At a retained first cell, replacing the polynomial by P/Q preserves its exact
denominator exponent whenever all sampled Q values are p-adic units.
label: quotient_first_cell
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.quotient_first_cell

doc:
Clean moduli for arbitrary rational samples whose denominators clear with a
linear bit budget. The denominator may involve factors unrelated to the index.
label: sample_modulus
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.sample_modulus

doc:
For nonmonomial Q, a fixed prime support for its retained values and p-adic
unit values at the selected prime suffice for the same window bound.
label: quotient_window_bound
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.quotient_window_bound

doc: Split a fixed denominator into a coprime grid and factors absorbed after a fixed delay.
label: split_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.split_denominator

doc:
For any chosen clearing denominator, its part prime to b is the grid denominator
in both maximal cases of the integral classification.
label: rational_grid
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.rational_grid

doc:
For an arbitrary rational polynomial, positive pole order after cancellation
is the only algebraic hypothesis in the bounded-gap discrepancy theorem.
label: rational_pole_bound
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.rational_pole_bound

doc:
Every rational polynomial in either integral-classification maximal case
is nonnormal on every mask; some positive reciprocal grid gap persists.
label: rational_boundary
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.rational_boundary

doc:
Binary shifts near the two nonzero thirds on clean blocks have limiting
discrepancy 2/3. The sharp binary transition inequality supplies the upper bound.
label: thirds_discrepancy
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.thirds_discrepancy

doc: The full ternary support with polynomial X²/3 and denominator m.
label: ternary_linear_thirds
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.ternary_linear_thirds

doc:
The full dyadic support, weighted by 1/(3m), also has discrepancy 2/3.
At the common binary depth 2ʲ+j the numerator is 2 modulo 3 for every j≥1.
label: dyadic_reciprocal_thirds
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.dyadic_reciprocal_thirds

doc:
Lower bound through *every* cutoff for selected windows [uᵢ,2uᵢ).
Only the maximum ratio of successive left endpoints enters the bound.
label: bounded_ratio_count
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.bounded_ratio_count

doc:
Arbitrary smooth masks with eventually bounded gaps between retained power
exponents. The numerator is rational, signed, and has no degree bound.
label: bounded_gap_discrepancy
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.bounded_gap_discrepancy

doc: A single model orbit accurate only on the given block suffices.
label: interval_block
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.interval_block

doc:
The density of positions with certified growing denominators controls
the full interval discrepancy. The rational weights may be arbitrary.
label: discrepancy_of_windows
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.discrepancy_of_windows

doc: Polynomial coefficient growth gives absolute summability after radix discounting.
label: summable_weight
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.summable_weight

doc:
On blocks of length B at height O(B²), a forward gap of length B
makes the signed shifted tail uniformly small.
label: gap_approximation
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.gap_approximation

doc:
Transfer estimates on blocks with a forward and backward gap, charging
uncontrolled positions individually up to the actual cutoff.
label: transfer
name: NormalityChecker.PolynomialMasks.transfer

doc:
With only base primes, the orbit spends density zero in every compact
subinterval of `(0,1)`. This includes the empty support.
label: interior_frequency_zero
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.interior_frequency_zero

doc: Maximal discrepancy when all support primes divide the radix.
label: maximal_of_base_primes
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.maximal_of_base_primes

doc: Complete classification of maximal discrepancy for finite prime support.
label: maximal_discrepancy_iff
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.maximal_discrepancy_iff

doc: Every finite prime support containing two gives normality in every odd base.
label: normal_of_two_mem
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.normal_of_two_mem

doc:
For a fixed denominator cutoff, bad full-block starts occupy a vanishing
fraction of each cell. A single prime divisor of `c` detects separation.
label: exceptional_of_separated
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.Composite.Generators.exceptional_of_separated

doc: Common clearing, insertion and orbit argument for all signed numerators.
label: normal_weighted
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.Composite.Generators.normal_weighted

doc: Positive orders with unit numerator.
label: normal
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.Composite.Generators.normal

doc: The same result with the series and all generator assumptions written out.
label: series_normal
name: NormalityChecker.Localized.Composite.Generators.series_normal

doc:
Among words in an alphabet of size `a`, words with at most `k` occurrences
of the distinguished symbol have total count at most `(2*a-1)^j / 2^(j-k)`.
For orbit models each symbol records two consecutive radix digits.
label: few_symbol_words
name: NormalityChecker.few_symbol_words

doc:
On a block of length `n`, the total first-frequency deficit at numerator
one is at most `2π (2^n-1)/Q`.
label: unit_numerator_escape
name: NormalityChecker.unit_numerator_escape

doc:
At every positive index at least one of the two consecutive actual
model denominators admits a reduced numerator with total deficit at most `4π`.
label: adjacent_small_escape
name: NormalityChecker.adjacent_small_escape

doc:
A finite van der Corput estimate with stride `v`. Only correlations of

On every sufficiently late scale the reduced denominator retains all but

name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.retained_denominator

A leading monomial retaining its full denominator exponent up to bounded loss
survives any rational combination of strictly lower-degree monomials.
label: rational_sum_normal_of_retention
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.rational_sum_normal_of_retention

doc: The error is the actual shifted tail of the square, summed over ordered pairs.
label: shifted_tail
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamSquare.shifted_tail

doc:
All four intervals include the left endpoint. The exponent labels in this
statement use `k+4` for the logarithmic scale, hence cover every scale from 4 on.

doc: The second interval on the third scale is a genuine small-scale exception.
label: third_scale_exception
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamSquare.third_scale_exception

doc:
Exact initial denominator profile, including every digit in the exceptional
third scale and the empty prefixes before the first insertion.
label: initial_profile
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamSquare.initial_profile

doc: The reduced prefix denominators grow quadratically at every late digit.
label: quadratic_denominator
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamSquare.quadratic_denominator

doc: The square of the Stoneham series starting at exponent one is binary normal.
label: binary_normal
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamSquare.binary_normal

doc:
Modulo the rotation prime, an invariant sum on words of prime-power length
reduces to its constant words. Apply the fixed-point congruence on each fiber.
label: sum_eq_diagonal_of_prime_power
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.sum_eq_diagonal_of_prime_power

doc:
In prime-power dimension, binary mass stabilizes at an integer whose
residue modulo the degree prime is minus two to the first occupied diagonal index.
label: symmetric_binary_mass
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.symmetric_binary_mass

doc:
A single binary precision works for all symmetric upper sets containing a
given constant point, when their dimension is a power of an odd prime.
label: symmetric_binary_uniform_precision
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.symmetric_binary_uniform_precision

doc:
In the index-zero normalization the coefficient precision depends only
on the distinguished monomial, uniformly over integral perturbations of no
larger degree.
label: tied_axis_normal
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.tied_axis_normal

doc:
Fix any finite list of standard monomials of at most the top degree.
After multiplying their integer coefficients by a sufficiently high common
power of p, every combination with the distinguished monomial is normal.
label: tied_standard_normal
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.tied_standard_normal

doc:
A one-step radix dilation gives an exact affine dependence between
distinct standard generators. This produces ties with complete cancellation.
label: radix_stride_identity
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.radix_stride_identity

doc: Independent formulation using the standard series and positive parameters.
label: tied_coefficient_statement
name: NormalityChecker.StonehamPolynomial.tied_coefficient_statement

doc: Prime-band cancellation for any integer-weight recurrence invariant under multiplying the index by p.
label: weighted_short_regular
name: NormalityChecker.StrideDenominatorRate.weighted_short_regular

doc: Test on the actual short numerator, valid on every large-prime band.
label: weighted_prime_survives
name: NormalityChecker.StrideDenominatorRate.weighted_prime_survives

doc: Removing the p-indexed short prefix leaves a rational which is integral at p.
label: short_prefix_regular
name: NormalityChecker.StrideDenominatorRate.short_prefix_regular

doc: Test on the actual short numerator, valid on every large-prime band.
label: prime_survives
name: NormalityChecker.StrideDenominatorRate.prime_survives

doc: All primes in (N/K,N/2] survive for every sufficiently late N at fixed K.
label: band_survival
name: NormalityChecker.StrideDenominatorRate.band_survival

doc: The floor in the digit cutoff contributes a vanishing normalized error.
label: floor_ratio
name: NormalityChecker.StrideDenominatorRate.floor_ratio

doc: The actual reduced denominator of the half-length model has logarithmic rate 1/2.
label: log_denominator_rate
name: NormalityChecker.StrideDenominatorRate.log_denominator_rate

doc:
A weighted sum of distinct simple fractions takes any prescribed value at
most as often as there are poles, provided one residue survives.
label: simple_fraction_fiber
name: NormalityChecker.StrideResidueReturns.simple_fraction_fiber

doc:
In a single residue class of the coefficient period, at most h positions
in a prime block have any given ordered pair of regular residues at distance h.
The numerator condition excludes gaps consisting entirely of zero coefficients.
label: regular_pairs
name: NormalityChecker.StrideResidueReturns.regular_pairs

doc: From fixed-gap collisions to the number of hits in an arbitrary short interval.
label: window_of_pairs
name: NormalityChecker.StrideResidueReturns.window_of_pairs

doc:
Anti-concentration in each phase class of a periodically weighted prefix.
Different multiples of p may lie before the observation window.
label: regular_window
name: NormalityChecker.StrideResidueReturns.regular_window

doc:
A common numerator and an invertible denominator simultaneously represent
the rational prime-free sum and its finite-field value.
label: actual_regular_digit
name: NormalityChecker.StrideResidueReturns.actual_regular_digit

doc:
Any given residue occurs at most six times the one-phase bound in T positions
of any p-block of the actual two-stride p-regular digits.
label: logarithm_window
name: NormalityChecker.StrideResidueReturns.logarithm_window

doc: The two series have digit exponents 2j and 3j.
label: logTwo_two_stride_series
name: NormalityChecker.logTwo_two_stride_series

doc:
The smaller-denominator prefix follows every true binary shift, with an explicit
one-sided error.
label: twoStridePrefix_tail
name: NormalityChecker.twoStridePrefix_tail

doc: At these primes exactly one term of the two-stride prefix has a pole.
label: twoStridePrefix_survival
name: NormalityChecker.twoStridePrefix_survival

doc:
First-frequency escape at an integer multiple gives a quantitative lower
bound on first-frequency escape at the original point.
label: cosineEscape_multiple
name: NormalityChecker.cosineEscape_multiple

doc: Uniform bounds for interval discrepancy in every integer base.
label: radix_discrepancy_bounds
name: NormalityChecker.radix_discrepancy_bounds

doc: A vanishing sequence of uniform discrepancy upper bounds gives digit normality.
label: normal_of_radix_limsup_zero
name: NormalityChecker.normal_of_radix_limsup_zero

doc:
A single cutoff works for all intervals and all sufficiently large clean
orbits. `M` is a cutoff for the reduced denominator at the start of the block.
label: smooth_interval_block
name: NormalityChecker.smooth_interval_block

doc:
On every clean block the reduced denominator at a later position divides
the starting denominator. One surviving position suffices for the full block.
label: discrepancy_of_survival
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.discrepancy_of_survival

doc:
Finite Poincaré recurrence supplies a positive-measure common event for all
subset combinations of the chosen rotations. Each return time can be arbitrarily large.
label: positive_intersection_cube
name: NormalityChecker.ThresholdDifferences.positive_intersection_cube

doc:
If two exponents agree after the preperiod, the matching terms cancel
at every larger q-exponent, with any other cofactor u.
label: stabilized_weight
name: NormalityChecker.ThresholdDifferences.stabilized_weight

doc:
A finite union of translates of a fixed real lattice has a gap around zero,
allowing zero itself. This is applied to differences of log thresholds in nearby rows.
label: finite_ray_gap
name: NormalityChecker.ThresholdDifferences.finite_ray_gap

doc:
The integral for ln 2 gives a block of `T-1` consecutive starts with at least
one change, for every late `B` and `2 ≤ T ≤ B`.
label: logTwo_one_change_blocks
name: NormalityChecker.TransitionWindows.logTwo_one_change_blocks

doc:
The corrected numerator at `N` certifies individual true transitions through
two further shell lengths by a fixed interior test on its rational orbit.
label: logTwo_hit_of_diagonal
name: NormalityChecker.TransitionWindows.logTwo_hit_of_diagonal

doc:
Two four-bit CRT cells suffice to force a true transition. The equality of
fractional parts follows from the CRT identity for the chosen numerator.
label: logTwo_hit_of_crt_cells
name: NormalityChecker.TransitionWindows.logTwo_hit_of_crt_cells

doc:
Each transition is charged at most once per internal offset. The last possible
transition is at `2*N+T-3` when `N≥1` and `T≥2`.
label: aggregate_le
name: NormalityChecker.TransitionWindows.aggregate_le

doc:
For every sufficiently large dyadic shell suppose the mean number of changes
per word is at least `α*T`, for any positive word length at most the shell size.
The frequency bound holds at every sufficiently large integer cutoff.
label: frequency_of_dyadic_aggregate
name: NormalityChecker.TransitionWindows.frequency_of_dyadic_aggregate

doc:
Positive aggregate on all late dyadic shells gives a positive lower density
and an explicit strict bound on the upper limiting interval discrepancy.
label: density_discrepancy_of_dyadic_aggregate
name: NormalityChecker.TransitionWindows.density_discrepancy_of_dyadic_aggregate

doc:
The requested power-length criterion for the actual binary words of ln 2.
The case `δ=1` permits words extending almost a full shell past its right edge.
label: logTwo_of_many_rich_windows
name: NormalityChecker.TransitionWindows.logTwo_of_many_rich_windows

doc: Every rational orbit misses a fixed positive-length interval between grid nodes.
label: rational_discrepancy_pos
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.rational_discrepancy_pos

doc:
A length-L cyclic word with exactly one visit to each L-cell has positive
discrepancy at most 2/L. Order-k de Bruijn words satisfy the count for L=b^k.
label: de_bruijn_discrepancy_bounds
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.de_bruijn_discrepancy_bounds

doc: The binary word 00010111 has one cyclic occurrence of every three-bit word.
label: de_bruijn_eight_cells
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.de_bruijn_eight_cells

doc:
Rational translations by inverse powers of any fixed integer coprime to the
base have discrepancy tending to zero as their denominator grows.
label: inverse_power_discrepancy_tendsto
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.inverse_power_discrepancy_tendsto

doc:
One fixed signed expansion with positive discrepancy yields arbitrarily small
strictly positive discrepancies by explicitly adding inverse powers of `t`.
label: arbitrarily_small_translations
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.arbitrarily_small_translations

doc:
Numerical discrepancy can change after division by nine, even for the
explicit nonnormal transcendental example with alternating phases.
label: division_by_nine_example
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.division_by_nine_example

doc:
All prefix discrepancies of a rational converge to the discrepancy of one
complete period of its eventual orbit.
label: rational_discrepancy_limit
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.rational_discrepancy_limit

doc:
With either sign of nonzero integer dilation and every rational translation,
the error in the weighted rational orbit discrepancy tends to zero over all cutoffs.
label: translated_discrepancy
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.translated_discrepancy

doc:
Multiplication of the two upper discrepancies, for every bounded signed
phase sequence and every rational translation.
label: translated_limsup
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.translated_limsup

doc: Translation by one third of the three binary periodic phase examples.
label: translated_third_examples
name: NormalityChecker.SignedPhases.translated_third_examples

doc: Exact finite conservation law, including both endpoint terms.
label: cosineSpike_sum
name: NormalityChecker.cosineSpike_sum

doc:
A finite transition inequality. The free positive parameter trades the
second-moment allowance against the mass of the transition interval.
label: spike_transition_bound
name: NormalityChecker.spike_transition_bound

doc:
An eventual upper bound on the second moment with arbitrary positive slack
is the usual finite limsup hypothesis, including eventual boundedness.
label: transition_of_spike_moment
name: NormalityChecker.transition_of_spike_moment

doc: A first-moment tail allowance suffices. It can be tested at a single finite cutoff.
label: transition_of_spike_excess
name: NormalityChecker.transition_of_spike_excess

doc: Double counting prime failures on an arbitrary interval uses its length in the spacing bound.
label: window_lost_weight
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.window_lost_weight

doc: Specialization to an initial segment (with the coarser common scale `2*N`).
label: total_lost_weight
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.total_lost_weight

doc: All surviving primes in `(n,2n]` divide the reduced denominator.
label: diagonal_weight_lower
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.diagonal_weight_lower

doc: The aggregate log weight lost by all diagonal models is `o(N²)`.
label: mean_lost_weight
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.mean_lost_weight

doc:
For every positive fractional tolerance the diagonal models whose logarithmic
prime loss exceeds that fraction of `n` have natural density zero.
label: lost_primes_density_zero
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.lost_primes_density_zero

doc:
For each `ε>0`, the fully corrected denominators exceed `exp((1-ε)n)`
outside a set of indices of natural density zero.
label: diagonal_small_denominators_density_zero
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.diagonal_small_denominators_density_zero

doc:
For each fixed positive fraction, the indices losing that fraction of the
primes in `(n,2n]` have natural density zero.
label: missing_prime_fraction_density_zero
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.missing_prime_fraction_density_zero

doc: On the fundamental interval, each fiber of a finite-ray moment is finite.
label: finite_ray_fiber
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.finite_ray_fiber

doc:
With no cofactor prime at all, the first row is a unit and the tail is
divisible by p. In particular the actual unsigned moment never vanishes here.
label: phaseMoment_empty_ne_zero
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.phaseMoment_empty_ne_zero

doc:
For *each* off-radix support prime, the infinite intersection of the
checker's failed regions has Lebesgue measure zero, in every positive order.
label: unsigned_persistent_null
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.unsigned_persistent_null

doc: Twice the total failed-cell width bounds the worst-prefix score, at every order.
label: certificate_le_twice_mass
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.certificate_le_twice_mass

doc:
The computable worst-prefix certificate tends to zero for every individual
off-base prime. The conclusion allows a positive certificate at every finite depth.
label: unsigned_certificate_tendsTo_zero
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.unsigned_certificate_tendsTo_zero

doc:
Every unsigned full finite-prime expansion with an off-base prime is normal
in its defining radix, at every positive denominator order.
label: unsigned_finite_support_normal
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.unsigned_finite_support_normal

doc:
Along every prefix, interval discrepancy tends to one for all-base
supports and to zero for supports containing an off-base prime.
label: unsigned_discrepancy_limit
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.unsigned_discrepancy_limit

doc:
At phases below one the first row is empty. Scaling up by a power of the
selected prime therefore preserves zeros as long as the final phase is below p.
label: moment_scale_down
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.moment_scale_down

doc: Exact cofactor difference on the actual infinite weighted phase.
label: moment_difference
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.moment_difference

doc:
Finite-ray moments separate any two sufficiently close log phases, uniformly
in their location. The bare ray supplies an actual jump in every open interval.
label: finite_ray_separation
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.finite_ray_separation

doc:
Recurrence chooses a positive multiple of any prescribed stride. The shifted
representative can cross the end of the log circle.
label: positiveZeros_difference
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.positiveZeros_difference

doc:
Powers can have a preperiod when q shares a prime with D. Every positive
multiple of the resulting stride can be used as a return time.
label: cofactor_stride
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.cofactor_stride

doc: One round of differencing bounds the exponent of q by L+a-1.
label: difference_tail
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.difference_tail

doc:
For an unsigned moment, an equality between two powers of the actual
Teichmüller factor suffices to truncate one cofactor exponent, even when the
chosen stride is shorter than a period for all residues modulo p−1.
label: phaseMoment_truncated_difference
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.Unsigned.phaseMoment_truncated_difference

doc:
A bad full block costs its length. A nonnegative charge on good blocks is
summed only over observations actually present in the prefix.
label: charged_prefix_bound
name: NormalityChecker.charged_prefix_bound

doc:
Transfer a local bound to all prefix lengths, uniformly over a family of
observables (for example, all intervals). The cutoff and errors may depend on the support.
label: transfer_clean_blocks
name: NormalityChecker.LocalizedSupport.transfer_clean_blocks

doc: For each fixed tolerance the small diagonal denominators have upper Banach density zero.
label: small_denominators_uniformly_sparse
name: NormalityChecker.ShadowCancellations.small_denominators_uniformly_sparse
